root_cause.mechanism: The `_normalize` function, introduced to adhere to PEP 685, calls `canonicalize_name` on values when the environment key is "extra". However, it failed to account for the fact that `extra` can be passed as `None` in the environment, causing `canonicalize_name` (which expects a string) to raise a `TypeError`.

hypotheses.text: The bug is caused by `_normalize` in `src/packaging/markers.py` calling `canonicalize_name` on `None` when `key == "extra"`. If I modify `_normalize` to handle `None` by converting it to an empty string, the error will be resolved.
hypotheses.predicts: The reproduction script will pass and print False.
hypotheses.evidence: The reproduction script now prints False instead of raising TypeError.

hypotheses.text: The bug is in `canonicalize_name` in `src/packaging/utils.py`, which should handle `None` input. If I modify `canonicalize_name` to handle `None`, the error will be resolved.
hypotheses.predicts: The reproduction script will still fail with the same TypeError.
hypotheses.evidence: The fix in markers.py resolved the issue, so the fix in utils.py is not needed.

patch.diff:
diff --git a/src/packaging/markers.py b/src/packaging/markers.py
index a5bf35c..6e2177a 100644
--- a/src/packaging/markers.py
+++ b/src/packaging/markers.py
@@ -121,7 +121,7 @@ def _normalize(*values: str, key: str) -> Tuple[str, ...]:
     # > When comparing extra names, tools MUST normalize the names being
     # > compared using the semantics outlined in PEP 503 for names
     if key == "extra":
-        return tuple(canonicalize_name(v) for v in values)
+        return tuple(canonicalize_name(v if v is not None else "") for v in values)
 
     # other environment markers don't have such standards
     return values
